subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Uncle Tom's Cabin and the Abolition Movement
description: A micro-lesson that makes Uncle Tom's Cabin and the Abolition Movement usable.

hook.text: When Abraham Lincoln met Harriet Beecher Stowe, he reportedly called her the little woman who started a war.

buildup.text: Published in 1852, Uncle Tom's Cabin depicted the brutal reality of slavery for Northern readers.

discovery.text: The novel sold three hundred thousand copies in its first year, an unprecedented number for the era.

twist.text: Southern states banned the book, and pro-slavery authors wrote dozens of novels trying to refute it.

climax.text: The novel galvanized anti-slavery sentiment across the North and became fuel for the Civil War.

punchline.text: A novel helped ignite a war that freed millions.

quiz.question: What impact did Uncle Tom's Cabin have on American society?
options: It galvanized anti-slavery sentiment and fueled the Civil War
